Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **One table of actions**: keys, controller buttons, swipes and right-button drags, the quick menu and the controls list all run the same actions, and the player rebinds them in Change Controls (a key or a button for each action, a swipe, and which buttons the quick menu shows), kept over the game's own
- **A quick menu that keeps out of the way**: the message window's buttons as a strip that fades in near the pointer (a tap on its handle on a phone), dimmed while an action can't be done and lit while it's on, with a pin, a larger size for fingers and an opacity of the player's choosing; the sample's message-window buttons are its quick menu now
- **Tips**: a button's hint shows beside the pointer resting on it, or under the focus at once (the SDL engine's window showed none); the quick menu's buttons tell what they do, and the sample's Config tabs what each page holds
- **Scrolling lists**: a list or grid that scrolls with the wheel, by dragging (a flick coasts on), with its bar, the keys or a controller (`KAGScrollList`); the sample's Search shows what it finds in one, and its backlog coasts after a flick
- **The screen, the controller and screenshots in Config**: the window's size, how full screen fills a screen of another shape, smooth scaling, vsync, the controller on or off, screenshots with or without the message window and as PNG or JPEG; a game can name its screenshots, stamp a watermark on them and turn them off for a scene (`[screenshot enabled=false]`)
- **Reduce Motion** stills actions and `.asd` animations too; Config has a movie volume of its own; the engine-drawn screens play hover sounds
- **Fixed**: `[ai far]` and `[ai near]` with an angry or sad face showed the picture before in the far or near place; a screen opened during the title's crossfade stopped for good
- kagex-release 0.19.0 downloads the 0.19.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.19.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
